title: Equitable Hiring & Accessibility Standards
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary:

This document defines Redwood Inference's standards for equitable hiring, interview accessibility, and inclusive onboarding adjustments. It sets mandatory practices for job postings, interviewing panels, accommodation handling, and manager responsibilities during the first 90 days. The goal is to reduce bias, increase access for candidates and employees with disabilities, and ensure consistent, traceable handling of accommodation requests.

Scope and audience:
- Applies to all hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, recruiters, and people managers responsible for onboarding new hires across Redwood Inference.
- Covers external candidates, internal transfers, reboarding (returning from leave), and contractors converting to full-time employees.

Guiding principles:
1) Accessibility-first: Make the default experience accessible rather than offering accommodations as an afterthought.
2) Structure reduces bias: Use job-focused rubrics and structured interviews for all technical and role-critical interviews.
3) Timely & confidential: Acknowledge accommodation requests within 2 business days and protect candidate privacy.
4) Reasonable & pragmatic: Provide reasonable accommodations promptly unless there is a documented business constraint; consult Legal only for edge cases.

Job posting & sourcing checklist (mandatory):
- Use clear, inclusive language: prefer "required" only for non-negotiable skills; otherwise use "preferred". Avoid gendered phrasing.
- Accessibility statement: Add the standard paragraph below to every posting.
  "Redwood Inference is committed to building an inclusive hiring process. If you need accommodations during the application or interview process, please contact accommodations@redwood.ai or reply to your recruiter; we will respond within 2 business days."
- Minimum hiring timeline published in posting: "Typical process: application → phone screen (7 days) → on-site/loop (within 14 days) → offer (target 28 days)."
- Sourcing: track outreach channels and include at least one underrepresented talent source (university programs, affinity groups, community orgs) for every open role above IC2 / L3.

Structured interview & rubric standards (required):
- Every role must define 3–5 core competencies used to evaluate candidates (examples: system design, problem solving, collaboration, impact).
- Create a scorecard with behavioral anchors for scores 1–5 for each competency.
- Interviewers must complete scorecards within 24 hours of the interview.
- Offer threshold: candidates must meet or exceed the minimum on at least 2/3 core competencies and not score below 2 on any essential competency.
- Panel composition guidance: at least 2 interviewers per loop, diverse by team/function where feasible; include a hiring manager and a peer. Consider cross-team representation for senior roles.

Bias mitigation & interviewer training:
- Annual mandatory training for all interviewers: structured interviewing, unconscious bias, disability etiquette.
- Interviewers should avoid asking about medical history or disability during interviews. Instead, ask work-relevant questions and offer accommodations.
- Use anonymized resume review for high-volume roles when possible.

Accommodation request handling (process):
1) Candidate or employee submits request to accommodations@redwood.ai or tells recruiter/manager.
2) People-ops acknowledges receipt within 2 business days and logs a confidential accommodation ticket (internal ID).
3) People-ops coordinates with the hiring manager and recruiter to propose reasonable accommodations within 3 business days of acknowledgement.
4) If the accommodation requires third-party services (ASL interpreter, assistive tech), people-ops will coordinate procurement and cover costs.
5) Confirm accommodation in writing and document any agreed timeline changes to the interview loop.

Common accommodations and recommended options:
- Extended coding assignment time (e.g., +50%).
- Remote interview by default on request (video or phone).
- Option for screen-reader-friendly materials, accessible slide decks, transcripts, and alt-text on images.
- ASL interpreter or real-time captioning for interviews.
- Sensory-friendly interview slots (shorter sessions, extra breaks, low-video options).

Confidentiality and recordkeeping:
- Accommodation requests are stored in a secure HR system with restricted access (people-ops and the hiring manager only).
- Do not include accommodation details in candidate-facing offer letters unless necessary and consented to.

Onboarding & reboarding standards (first 90 days):
- Pre-boarding (before day 1): confirm accommodation needs and provide an accessibility checklist tailored to the role (hardware, software, environment).
- Day 0 checklist for people managers: confirm meeting preferences, calendar visibility, preferred communication channels, and any assistive tech set-up.
- Buddy assignment: assign a peer buddy trained in accessibility-aware onboarding within the first week.
- 30/60/90 plan: managers co-create the plan with the new hire in week 1, explicitly noting any adjustments (e.g., extended timelines for training tasks).
- Reboarding flow (return from extended leave): conduct a "reboard" meeting 7 days prior to return when feasible to review any workplace adjustments.

Performance review & feedback adjustments:
- Use the same structured competency-based rubric used in hiring for performance reviews to increase consistency.
- At performance review kickoff, managers must ask if any accommodations are needed for the review process itself (format, timing, support person).
- Calibration: people-ops will include an accessibility lens in calibration cycles to identify possible bias against candidates/employees who use accommodations (e.g., different communication cadence).
- Reasonable adjustments to development plans or timelines should be documented in the employee's development plan; do not equate accommodations with lowered expectations—clarify objective performance criteria and adjusted support.

Manager guide: first 30 / 60 / 90 day checklist (short):
- Day 0–7:
  1. Confirm accessibility needs and schedule technical setup with IT.
  2. Introduce buddy and schedule daily check-ins for week 1.
  3. Share 30/60/90 draft and review with new hire; incorporate preferred communication cadence.
- Day 8–30:
  1. Ensure training materials are available in accessible formats.
  2. Hold weekly 1:1 focused on role clarity and friction removal.
  3. Collect feedback from buddy and update onboarding actions.
- Day 31–90:
  1. Move from onboarding to development goals; set measurable deliverables.
  2. Schedule mid-probation check-in at day 60.
  3. Confirm whether further accommodations or adjustments are needed.

Operational metrics & targets (recommended):
- Time-to-offer target: median <= 28 calendar days from screening of qualified candidate.
- Accommodation acknowledgment SLA: 2 business days; accommodation resolution target: within 5 business days for common requests.
- Interview scorecard completion: >= 95% within 24 hours.
- Return-to-work reboarding meeting scheduled >= 7 days before return for 90% of cases.
- Candidate satisfaction (post-process survey): target NPS >= 30 for candidates who request accommodations.

Escalation & edge cases:
- If an accommodation imposes undue hardship or a legal conflict, people-ops will escalate to Legal and the Head of People for a decision within 5 business days.
- If a manager or interviewer violates confidentiality or mishandles an accommodation, report to people-ops immediately; incidents will be investigated and may lead to remedial training or disciplinary action.

Templates & examples (appendix):
- Accommodation acknowledgement email (template):
  "Hi [Name],

  Thanks for letting us know about your accommodation needs. We received your request on [date] and will follow up with proposed arrangements by [date+3 business days]. If you prefer to discuss by phone, please let us know a convenient time.

  Regards,
  People Ops"

- Interviewer scorecard sample (text table):
  Competency | 1 (low) | 3 (meets) | 5 (exceeds)
  Problem Solving | Candidate struggles to decompose problems | Candidate decomposes and proposes reasonable solutions | Candidate proposes elegant solutions and tradeoffs

Ownership & next steps:
- Document owner: People Operations (Maya Chen).
- Review cadence: Annual review in Q4 each year or sooner if legislation or company policy changes.
- Immediate rollout: people-ops to run a 4-week pilot with two engineering teams (Infra and Serving Runtime) starting 2026-03-01 to validate timelines and accommodations procurement flows.
